title: Ambient categories and small subcategories
statement:
For a scheme $T$, adopt exactly the ambient and small category constructions of [def-sf-categories], with the following notation and coefficient conventions.

Choose $\tau=\mathrm{\acute et}$ or $\mathrm{pro\acute et}$ and a sheaf of commutative rings $R_T$ on the corresponding small site $T_\tau$. The ambient categories are
$$
D(T_\tau,R_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)),\qquad
D^+(T_\tau,R_T),\quad D^-(T_\tau,R_T),\quad D^b(T_\tau,R_T).
$$
Here $\operatorname{Mod}(R_T)$ is the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules, $D$ is its ordinary derived category, and the three full subcategories consist respectively of objects with cohomology vanishing in sufficiently negative degrees, in sufficiently positive degrees, and outside a finite interval. For a set of primes $P$ invertible on $T$, $D^+_{P\text{-tor}}(T_\tau,R_T)$ is the full subcategory of $D^+(T_\tau,R_T)$ on the objects $K$ such that every element $x$ in every geometric stalk of every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^i(K)$ has a positive annihilator $m$ all of whose prime divisors lie in $P$. The stalk is taken on the chosen site. This is a condition on cohomology stalk groups.

For the coefficient stages, fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\ge1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Require $\ell$ invertible on $T$ when using the finite-Tor conventions. For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, on either chosen site the small categories are
$$
D^b_c(T_\tau,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b(T_\tau,\Lambda),\qquad
D^b_{ctf}(T_\tau,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b_c(T_\tau,\Lambda),\qquad
D_c^{[a,b]}(T_\tau,\Lambda)\subseteq D^b_c(T_\tau,\Lambda)
$$
for integers $a\le b$. They consist, respectively, of bounded objects with constructible cohomology, of those objects having finite Tor amplitude, and of those objects with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$. Finite Tor amplitude means that there are integers $u\le v$ such that $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_T}M$ has cohomology only in $[u,v]$ for every degree-zero $\Lambda_T$-module sheaf $M$. Constructibility and tensor products are those on the specified site in [def-sf-categories]. All these subcategories have the morphisms, identities and composition of the containing category.

For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$, the ambient category is on the pro-etale site with completed ring sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=\varprojlim_j(A_{E,j})_T$. Its small category $D^b_c(T,\mathcal O_E)$ is the derived-complete category whose reductions are bounded constructible with one cohomological interval independent of $j$; $D^b_{ctf}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ additionally imposes one Tor interval independent of $j$. At the field stages,
$$
D^b_c(T,E)=D^b_c(T,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E],\qquad
D^b_c(T,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)=\mathop{\operatorname{2-colim}}_{E'}D^b_c(T,E'),
$$
where $E'$ runs over finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, using scalar localization and the common-stage category of [def-sf-categories]. Define $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ at these two field stages. At the three higher stages, $D_c^{[a,b]}$ denotes the full subcategory on the intersection of the shifted standard halves $D_c^{\ge a}\cap D_c^{\le b}$ specified there. The higher-stage constructions have these completed, localized and common-stage meanings; an identification with ordinary discrete constant-coefficient categories is not included.

I compared the item with that definition clause by clause: ambient D/D+/D-/Db of Mod(R_T) on either site; elementwise P-torsion on cohomology stalks of the chosen site; the A_{E,n} constructible/ctf/interval full subcategories with l invertible for ctf; the completed O_E pro-étale sheaf with uniform reduction intervals; scalar localization at E and the common-stage 2-colimit at Q̄_l, with ctf = c by definition; higher-stage intervals via the standard halves.
